claims.text: Fenton House began as a speculative development: William Eades built it in the 1680s intending to sell it on completion.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c05.
Do not imply its present appearance is wholly original.

claims.text: Fenton House's golden gates carry the cipher of Joshua and Anna Gee, residents from 1706 to 1730.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c05.
Supported in The house as a home; cipher legibility is not required for this stop.
The mapped entrance gate has not independently been identified as the particular golden gate.

claims.text: The Gees created Fenton House's extensive walled garden in the early eighteenth century; the National Trust identifies Joshua as a Quaker with American trade connections and links to William Penn.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c05; source locator The garden.
No precise commodity, transaction or exploitation story attributable to the gate or garden is established here.

claims.text: The New End complex included a workhouse built in 1849–50 and designed by H. E. Kendall, before its later hospital identity.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c08.
Different building phases must remain distinct.
The independent hospital-history page gives different early dates; use the official report's chronology with attribution rather than silently harmonising them.

claims.text: Historic England interprets New End's 1869 dispensary and infirmary as a shift from provision for destitution towards provision for sickness, and links their planning to contemporary reform.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c08.
Institutional interpretation, not a named patient's testimony.
The report associates narrow wards and tall windows with Nightingale's ideas; it does not say she designed the buildings.

claims.text: Charles Bell's 1884–85 circular ward tower at New End had three ward floors, each 50 feet across, accommodating 24 beds arranged radially against the outer wall.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c08.
The Rotunda is mapped behind the frontage, within the private estate.
Do not promise tower visibility or describe the street frontage as circular; this detail is optional contextual history, not the required visible anchor.

claims.text: Admiral's House's rooftop quarterdeck was added by Fountain North, whom the official history describes as a former naval captain rather than an admiral.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c07.
North lived there approximately 1775–1811; the property's name is not evidence of his rank.

claims.text: The claim that North fired rooftop cannons to celebrate naval victories is explicitly qualified as something he is said to have done.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c07.
Retain attribution and uncertainty; no invented witnessed firing or dialogue.

claims.text: The official history connects a print titled Admiral Barton's Hampstead with confusion over the house's identity, and says the Fortescues renamed it Admiral's House during their 1917–26 occupancy.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c07.
Distinguish earlier informal association from later renaming.

claims.text: The Society traces its beginnings to an offer of a telescope on condition that it be made available to the public; the Society formed in July 1899.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c06.
First-party institutional history.
The offered 10.5-inch reflector was not the later Cooke refractor.

claims.text: The observatory was established in 1910 above a newly constructed underground reservoir.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c06.
The history page gives this chronology; the current observatory page loosely calls the reservoir Victorian.
Do not repeat the unverified highest-point-in-London superlative.

claims.text: The Society reports observations of Halley's Comet from the observatory in both 1910 and 1986, with more than 1,000 public visitors on the latter return.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c06.
The number describes the 1986 return, not one night or current attendance.
No observing session is required or promised.

claims.text: The operator's pedestrian directions approach the observatory via a pedestrian gap near the south side of Whitestone Pond onto Hampstead Grove.
qualifications: Candidate hampstead-fresh-factory-c06.
Approach guidance does not grant daytime entry; current observing sessions require free booking and suitable weather.
